title: Unweighted triangle finding

problem.name: Unweighted triangle finding
problem.statement_latex:
Given oracle access to $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ for a simple undirected graph, find distinct $u,v,w$ with $A_{uv}A_{vw}A_{wu}=1$, or report that none exist. Triangles encode local clustering and small constraint witnesses.
The primary comparison counts adjacency-oracle queries; the explicit-input classical comparator counts arithmetic operations.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{5/4})$ queries, Le Gall\textquotesingle s combinatorial quantum-walk algorithm.
quantum.details_latex: The algorithm outputs a triangle with bounded error whenever one exists. The query count includes sampled neighborhoods and nested quantum walks. A circuit implementation additionally pays for updating and querying the stored subsets and neighborhoods.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n^{5/4})$ queries, Le Gall's combinatorial quantum-walk algorithm.
quantum.details_text: The algorithm outputs a triangle with bounded error whenever one exists. The query count includes sampled neighborhoods and nested quantum walks. A circuit implementation additionally pays for updating and querying the stored subsets and neighborhoods.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^2)$ entry queries; $O(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations, algebraic triangle detection.
classical.details_latex: Reading the matrix attains the classical query upper bound, and a hidden isolated triangle gives a quadratic worst-case query lower bound. Explicit-input triangle detection uses fast matrix multiplication with exponent $\omega\le9/4$, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$; sparse inputs permit additional combinatorial refinements.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant quantum walks require coherent subset registers and neighborhood data of polynomial size. A logical-qubit estimate depends on the stored-data representation and graph oracle; the query theorem itself fixes their query count.
